4.speaker: Symon Holl
4.text: “The company will be notified today and construction work will begin immediately after.”

5.speaker: Symon Holl
5.text: “Some in the Lotherberg Group will be pleased. The contract will be awarded to Underhall Construction.”

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: After a lengthy drive on cliffside roads, we arrived in Lenkurg. There, crowds of cheering citizens greeted us and the local government officials escorted us to the city hall.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: We were here for a significant meeting about the H-3 project. Several construction companies sent their representatives to the city hall.

8.speaker: Lileas Graf
8.text: “We'll not let the people or ourselves down. I won't let that happen to any of us.”

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Gus Manger couldn't make the meeting due to his visit to Rizia, but I had Symon Holl and Lileas Graf by my side.

10.speaker: Symon Holl
10.text: “Besides starting our economic recovery, this project will cut the time it takes to get here by road in half, Mr. President.”

11.speaker: Lileas Graf
11.text: “More importantly, it will lead to improvement in Agnland. I have lived with these people and seen them suffer.”

12.speaker: Lileas Graf
12.text: “I had to work with Underhall Construction before in Holsord. They accepted several contracts for the renovation of our central station and left much to be desired. The H-3 project shouldn't be left to them.”

13.speaker: Player
13.text: “I would like to hear your thoughts, Symon.”

16.speaker: Lileas Graf
16.text: “Well, one of our promises would be respected. We promised to focus on the planned economy to create jobs.”

19.speaker: Lileas Graf
19.text: “With the highway, we will be well on our way to economically strengthening this weak region."

21.speaker: Symon Holl
21.text: “I am glad to hear that. We should be able to slow down the recession if we finish this project successfully.”

22.speaker: Symon Holl
22.text: “According to my estimations this project will give about 50.000 citizens from Agnland employment.”

23.speaker: Lileas Graf
23.text: “I look forward to a positive financial outcome. According to my sources, we'll lift many people in these areas out of poverty.”

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: The meeting ended and we spent the remainder of the day attending events in Lenkurg.

25.speaker: Symon Holl
25.text: “If we are going to try a different company, this is the most unique.”

29.speaker: Symon Holl
29.text: “It would fit our election promises of switching to a free-market economy. Awarding contracts to privately owned corporations would be a step in the right direction.”

30.speaker: Symon Holl
30.text: “Taurus has completed fewer projects than the other companies. However, they are slightly faster and cheaper.”

31.speaker: Lileas Graf
31.text: “This company is completely private and directed by a non-government board. Do we even remember if they worked on a mega-project at all?”

37.speaker: Player
37.text: “Failure during this project is not an option.”

38.speaker: Player
38.text: “What kind of end results do we expect?”

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “What will it take to stop the recession?”

42.speaker: Symon Holl
42.text: “I am not too sure about trusting them with the contract but at least they have worked on several mega-projects and always delivered on time.”

43.speaker: Symon Holl
43.text: “Our economic revitalization plan is set to be a success. Failure is indeed not an option.”

44.speaker: Lileas Graf
44.text: “Out of all three, this is the company I trust the least. They seem to fail at respecting the contract terms of their workers. They're likely to cause trouble.”

45.speaker: Lileas Graf
45.text: “The underdeveloped cities of Lenkurg and Arvory will receive a lot more investment after this.”

46.speaker: Lileas Graf
46.text: “The SSC is one of our most trusted and honorable companies. They have served us a long time. I have worked with them on several occasions.”

47.speaker: Lileas Graf
47.text: “That depends on the government budget. We need to make sure we have enough money to fund critical ministries but still have enough left to invest.”

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: It was time to decide which company would be awarded the H-3 Highway contract.

49.speaker: Symon Holl
49.text: “Short-term employment and long-term economic development in the Nargis and Agnland regions.”

50.speaker: Lileas Graf
50.text: “They were only involved in smaller-scale regional projects. This doesn't prove their capabilities for larger undertakings that are more complex.”

51.speaker: Symon Holl
51.text: “Nonetheless, they subjected their workers to conditions beneath our standards during the Holsord Central Station contract. Which is troubling.”

52.speaker: Symon Holl
52.text: “I think that they have been doing relatively well in the private sector, where they are dominating the construction industry with successful projects.”

56.speaker: Lileas Graf
56.text: “There are other things Taurus does very well, like providing consultants for state corporations. But I can't vouch for their infrastructure construction at all.”

57.speaker: Symon Holl
57.text: “Not as of right now. However, things might come up if the project doesn't go according to plan.”

58.speaker: Symon Holl
58.text: “This is just the beginning. We will need to follow this project up with several other economic investments.”

60.speaker: Symon Holl
60.text: “Taurus Holding was founded in 1946 and is owned by the entrepreneur Geralt Fais.”

65.speaker: Lileas Graf
65.text: “It would fulfill your initial election promise of using a state-dominant planned economy to improve Sordland's bleak economic prospects.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “I don't feel confident about Taurus Holding.”

71.speaker: Symon Holl
71.text: “It goes against your election promises of moving away from a state-planned economy.”

76.speaker: Symon Holl
76.text: “Some in the Lotherberg Group won't like this. But the contract will be awarded to Taurus Holding.”

78.speaker: Lileas Graf
78.text: “I wish the outcome of this meeting was different. But at the end of the day, the success of the project is what matters.”

79.speaker: Symon Holl
79.text: “Most importantly the Sordish State Corporation uses outdated methods, resulting in slower construction.”

80.speaker: Lileas Graf
80.text: “I wish you had chosen differently. But at the end of the day, the success of the project is what matters.”

82.speaker: Lileas Graf
82.text: “I'm so glad that you have made this choice. I can tell from my experience that we will be very satisfied with this corporation.”

84.speaker: Lileas Graf
84.text: “They have the experience and the manpower to pull off a project like this.”

86.speaker: Symon Holl
86.text: “The outdated construction methods that they use concern me. They are several decades behind.”

87.speaker: Lileas Graf
87.text: “I don't agree with your negative statements, Symon. The SSC's record clearly shows completed contracts with thousands of employees who have more than 20 years of experience.”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “I am on the fence about the SSC.”

89.speaker: Player
89.text: “I like the SSC, but want to hear about the others.”

91.speaker: Symon Holl
91.text: “I have the overview of the companies here.”

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: Symon handed the files over to me.

93.speaker: Symon Holl
93.text: “The respected Sordish State Corporation, also known as the SSC was founded in 1891.”

98.speaker: Symon Holl
98.text: “The real estate and construction giant was founded in 1925 and expanded during the economic boom of the '30s.”

99.speaker: Lileas Graf
99.text: “According to them, the tight completion schedule necessitated such bad labor conditions. Which still doesn't justify the situation.”

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “I have settled on the SSC. [-2 Government Budget]”

101.speaker: Lileas Graf
101.text: “I reviewed them. I also took the liberty of asking the mayor of Arvory to give his opinion on the matter.”

103.speaker: Lileas Graf
103.text: “But during the station project, we had to extensively negotiate with the union so as to not lose a serious labor law violation case.”

104.speaker: Player
104.text: “I am not sure about Underhall Construction.”

105.speaker: Player
105.text: “Underhall seems interesting, but let's hear about the others.”

106.speaker: Player
106.text: “I have settled on Underhall Construction. [-2 Government Budget]”

114.speaker: Symon Holl
114.text: “My expectations are that the grand opening ceremony will happen late next year.”

115.speaker: Lileas Graf
115.text: “I'd better get back to work, then.”

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “I think we are off to a good start.”

118.speaker: Symon Holl
118.text: “It is the main state corporation tasked with running the day-to-day construction services of our country.”

119.speaker: Symon Holl
119.text: “The CEO of Underhall is Kris Schar, the mayor of Conriat. He sold half of his shares a few years ago.”

120.speaker: Symon Holl
120.text: “It is a new holding company whose subsidiaries use cutting-edge technology from Arcasia to reduce construction costs and prices. They are known to provide for their workers, who are part of the Labour Union of Sordland.”

121.speaker: Player
121.text: “Working conditions must be respected. This doesn't inspire confidence.”

122.speaker: Player
122.text: “We need to be able to trust the corporation. This is a base requirement for the contract.”

123.speaker: Lileas Graf
123.text: “I agree. The workers were undocumented Agnolian and Wehzek immigrants with no papers. A clear violation of our laws.”

124.speaker: Lileas Graf
124.text: “They indeed did work on three significant infrastructure projects.”

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “The experience they bring to the table is beneficial.”

126.speaker: Player
126.text: “The lack of a modern attitude is disappointing.”

127.speaker: Player
127.text: “The regional highway system has no relation to this.”

128.speaker: Player
128.text: “They do have a wealth of knowledge in infrastructure.”

129.speaker: Player
129.text: “The innovative aspect is refreshing. Especially if they can deliver.”

130.speaker: Player
130.text: “It seems like they lack the necessary experience.”

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “We shouldn't risk our first project. There is too much at stake here.”

132.speaker: Player
132.text: “Their capabilities matter more than the history they have. We need to make unbiased decisions.”

136.speaker: Symon Holl
136.text: “Picking this corporation would go against our planned economy policy.”

137.speaker: Symon Holl
137.text: “Picking this corporation would fit our market economy policy.”

138.speaker: Symon Holl
138.text: “Good that we are staying consistent to our economic strategy.”

148.speaker: Symon Holl

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: It was nice to enjoy the natural beauty of Agnland and to eat some good fish.

154.speaker: Lileas Graf
154.text: “Secondly, they are the only company to have worked in the Agnland region out of all three corporations.”

155.speaker: Symon Holl
155.text: “A simple look at the regional highways shows us the problem.”

156.speaker: Symon Holl
156.text: “It won several awards internationally for being one of the fastest growing and advanced companies.”

157.speaker: Lileas Graf
157.text: “Choosing this company is too much of a risk for such an important project, especially when a proven candidate like the SSC exists.”

169.speaker: Symon Holl
169.text: “Very well, Mr. President. The contract will be awarded to Underhall Construction.”

170.speaker: Symon Holl
170.text: “Very well, Mr. President. The contract will be awarded to Taurus Holding.”

171.speaker: Symon Holl
171.text: “Very well, Mr. President. The contract will be awarded to the Sordish State Corporation.”

172.speaker: Symon Holl
172.text: “Some in the Lotherberg Group won't like this, but the contract will be awarded to the Sordish State Corporation.”

173.speaker: Narrator
173.text: Symon signed a certain section of the dossier and fixed his glasses.

174.text: Symon signed a certain section of the dossier and fixed his glasses.

177.speaker: Symon Holl
177.text: “They took a joint contract in Arcasia for restructuring the highway intersection of one of the major cities. It went well but it is their only large-scale success.”

180.speaker: Narrator
180.text: Symon searched through the documents he was holding and found the one he was looking for.

198.speaker: Symon Holl
198.text: “According to the preliminary calculations of the SSC, they would need more resources to finish a project of this size.”

201.speaker: Symon Holl
201.text: “Underhall has specifically mentioned their solid track record and highlighted that they do anticipate to go over budget, but that the project will be finished on time.”

202.speaker: Symon Holl
202.text: “The project manager from Taurus Holding mentioned that they would be able to finish the project with the allocated funding. They are the only company who found the budget sufficient, making them a cheaper alternative.”
